title: Frontend: Modal In React
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Modal In React. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Open details[data-action=open] shows native dialog labelled Details. Close details[data-action=close] and Escape close it and restore trigger focus. [data-testid=closed] counts closes exactly once.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Centralize modal open state and use a native dialog or a proven accessible primitive.
alternativeApproaches: Handle stacked dialogs with explicit ownership rather than independent global key handlers.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Escape; backdrop policy; initial focus.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
